04/06.01.2026 Heard Mr. Srinivas Roy, learned counsel for the  appellant and learned Spl. P.P. assisted by Mr. N.K.
Chatterjee, learned counsel appearing for the informant.
This application has been preferred by the appellant for grant of bail to him during the pendency of this appeal.

The appellant has been convicted for the offences under Sections 376(2)(n), 313 and 506 IPC has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 10 years along with a fine of Rs. 5,000/- for the offence under Section 376(2)(n) IPC.

It has been alleged that the victim was allured by the appellant of providing her with a foothold in politics and also to open a Pragya Kendra and thereafter had taken her to a distant place where she was subjected to rape.

It has further been alleged that after committing rape, the victim was taken to the house of Samuel Samad which house was taken on rent by the appellant and in order to enable her to open a Pragya Kendra, had taken Rs. 50,000/- from her and also used to commit rape upon her by taking her to the jungle.

sentences.text: Submission has been advanced by the learned counsel for the appellant that the allegation itself appears to be absurd and improbable.
Learned counsel further submits that there was a delay of four months in institution of the FIR.
It has also been submitted that the evidence of the witnesses contradicts each other and in fact, the evidence of the victim does not cement the allegations made against the appellant.

Mr. N.K. Chatterjee, learned counsel appearing for the informant has opposed the prayer for bail and has referred to the evidence of the I.O., who has been examined as P.W.7 and has also referred to some of the witnesses who according to him are independent witnesses and have categorically supported the narration of the events made by the informant.

The entire sequence of events as depicted by the victim in her fardbeyan as well as in her evidence during trial seems to suggest that she was a consenting party to the sexual overtures made by the appellant.
The fardbeyan also reveals several absurdities which also demolishes the case of the prosecution.
The age of the victim has been assessed to be about 28 years.
The appellant was all along on bail during trial.
On consideration of the aforesaid fact, we are inclined to admit the appellant on bail.

Accordingly,
during pendency of this appeal, the appellant is directed to be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.10,000/- (Ten thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Additional Sessions Judge-I, Chaibasa in connection with S.T. No. 333/20222.
This application stands allowed.
However, any observation made by us with respect to the merits of the case shall be confined to this interlocutory application only.
I.A. No. 13920 of 2025 stands disposed of.
(Rongon Mukhopadhyay, J.) (Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, J.) Dated- 6th January, 2026.
Preet/-
